_law: Formats model FUNCTIONS, not people. A format owns ROLE SLOTS (see cast_logic.slots); the cast fills them. Never booking logic ('guest: true') - branch on whether a SLOT is filled. BRIGHT LINES are global (cast.json shared_rules) and override every format. Rendering (avatars/cameras/graphics/voice-EQ) is NOT here - it lives in production_skins.json and binds at render time. See FORMAT_SYSTEM.md.

enums.uncertainty_note: UNCERTAINTY is NOT a truth label - it is an orthogonal qualifier (uncertainty:true) on an ANALYSIS or PREDICTION claim.

slot_note: Each slot: {id, role (letter) or one_of (letters), required, substitution}. Multiplicity = multiple slots (panel_1, panel_2). one_of = a single seat that either role type can fill. substitution is MANDATORY for every slot (what replaces this human FUNCTION when the seat is empty); an abort substitution is a valid answer for SUBJECT_REQUIRED.

formats.name: MODERATED COLLISION
formats.reference: First Take (mechanics only, not the brand)

series_dna.spine: Turns the strongest live controversy into a direct collision between opposing positions.

slots.substitution: a host from the cast takes the moderator chair; if no neutral voice exists, downgrade to opinion-single
recurring co-host, rotating analyst, an AI advocate character, or a party's recorded stance
same pool as side_a; if truly no second voice exists, branch replaces opening-argument#2 with strongest-counterargument read by the moderator - never fake a debate

cast_logic.relationship_physics: adversarial (A vs B); moderator referees and never takes a side on air; debaters address each other by name, moderator addresses the audience

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: forced_choice - moderator plays the defining clip and asks a binary question

branches.note: moderator reads the strongest opposing case
side_a's rebuttal to the counterargument stands as the close

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: moderator shifts the question from abstract judgment to personal consequence ('would you tell them to walk away?')
episode_grammar.payoff: the moderator names who won the card, or the single dominant argument - always a verdict, never 'it depends whose card'
episode_grammar.close: one-line scorecard, then bell into the next card or out

formats.name: EVIDENCE MYSTERY
formats.reference: The Rachel Maddow Show - the investigative long-build mode (mechanics only)

series_dna.spine: Reconstructs the hidden chain of facts until a confusing event becomes understandable.

slots.substitution: recast the anchor from the cast pool; the show does not run without its anchor seat
OPTIONAL_PROOF: replace with a document walkthrough + timeline, a taped statement, or an extra reporting-block

cast_logic.relationship_physics: expert-surrogate - the proof seat confirms, supplies firsthand knowledge, or explains consequences; it never organizes the episode

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: mystery - open on something that looks unrelated (a forgotten announcement, an old promise, a contract clause)

branches.note: extra receipt instead of an interview

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: each added piece of evidence makes the original innocent explanation less plausible
episode_grammar.payoff: the opening clue becomes the key that unlocks the current story; every block ends one step short so the audience closes the loop
episode_grammar.close: the anchor's verdict + the single unresolved question to watch; out clean, no music tease
episode_grammar.notes: measured, never shouty - authority comes from the BUILD; direct address to the audience; rhetorical questions the anchor answers. Runs as a daily_bundle by chaining one build per story when the night has several.

series_dna.spine: Exposes the hypocrisy inside a public narrative, then lands a substantive point.

slots.substitution: recast the desk host from the cast pool
OPTIONAL: clip-montage + host commentary carries the same escalation
OPTIONAL_MODULE: drop the interview; run a desk-story instead

cast_logic.relationship_physics: straight-comic (host vs foil) and, when the interview seat is filled, interviewer-subject

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: joke - open on the funniest or most revealing clip
episode_grammar.escalation_curve: the foil takes the target's logic to an absurd extreme, or a montage proves reality is already more ridiculous than the joke
episode_grammar.payoff: the comedy gives way to a clear thesis (the host must land one real ANALYSIS/OPINION beat), or the interview exposes a more complicated reality
episode_grammar.close: callback joke to the cold open
episode_grammar.notes: the underlying facts must be supportable (FACT/ATTRIBUTED); only the FRAMING is SATIRE.

series_dna.spine: Explains an overlooked system, proves why it matters, names who benefits, and moves toward action.

slots.substitution: recast the host from the cast pool
NONE-critical: a prerecorded expert voice or an on-screen quotation; or cut the cameo entirely

cast_logic.relationship_physics: teacher-student (host to audience); cameos are flourishes, never load-bearing

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: strongest_clip then pivot - brief current hook, then into the real story
episode_grammar.escalation_curve: each example reveals the problem is the predictable OUTPUT of an incentive structure, not an isolated bad decision
episode_grammar.payoff: the audience sees the system, not just the headline - 'they are selling an escape from a problem they designed'
episode_grammar.close: the reform ask or audience action, punctuated by the spectacle

series_dna.spine: Strips a media-trained subject's persona through questions and an external challenge that escalate together.

slots.substitution: recast the host from the cast pool
ABORT: the subject IS the episode. No subject means no episode - select a different format, never fake it

cast_logic.relationship_physics: subject-interviewer under a shared, escalating external challenge

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: guest_ritual - introduce the subject, the rules, the progression, and the final challenge

branches.note: add rounds but keep the arc: origins -> career -> overlooked detail -> first controversy -> personal consequence -> public criticism -> regret -> hardest unresolved issue
SUBJECT_REQUIRED - pick a different episode or format

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: the external challenge (spicy food, gameplay difficulty, timed decisions, lie-detection, or archival clips) hardens as the questions get more consequential, in lockstep
episode_grammar.payoff: the subject drops the talking points and gives a raw, revealing, funny, or emotionally honest answer
episode_grammar.close: the final challenge and the direct answer to the hardest question

formats.name: HYBRID FORUM
formats.reference: Real Time with Bill Maher (mechanics only)

series_dna.spine: Frames the week, interrogates one major voice, stress-tests it through panel collision, and delivers a final editorial judgment.

slots.substitution: recast the host from the cast pool - this show is host-led
a senior panelist takes the one-on-one chair, or the host opens with a solo framing the panel then stress-tests - the interview module is core to this format
a generated panelist filling the competing-interpreter function
a generated panelist; if truly unavailable, run one strong voice vs the host and switch toward opinion-single
run the panel as a pair

cast_logic.relationship_physics: MULTI - interviewer-subject in the one-on-one, adversarial panel collision, host as final editorial authority; each module's people do DIFFERENT jobs

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: joke - opening monologue reacting to the week

branches.note: wrong format - switch to opinion-single or moderated-collision

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: private one-on-one claims get stress-tested live by the panel
episode_grammar.payoff: the host synthesizes or rejects the discussion in a polished final editorial

formats.name: OPEN PANEL
formats.reference: House format - our proven multi-host floor engine (was 'the-panel')

series_dna.spine: Puts the room's strongest voices on one controversy and argues it to a verdict.

slots.substitution: recast a lead voice from the cast pool
a generated peer host, or a party's recorded stance - a floor needs at least two voices
run as a two-hander; the allocator tightens turn-taking

cast_logic.relationship_physics: adversarial-cooperative peers (no formal moderator); disagreement engineered by the beat sheet, agreement earned

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: strongest_clip - hottest take commits in two sentences, show ID in one breath

branches.note: two-hander; uneven turn lengths, allocator tightens

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: turn lengths uneven (jabs beat paragraphs); interruptions land mid-clause; the withheld receipt detonates ON the floor and reframes the argument
episode_grammar.payoff: somebody lands a verdict + a weight-drop reframe; the exit is a tease, never a fade
episode_grammar.close: the button - prediction + comment challenge + tomorrow tease

formats.name: OPINION SINGLE
formats.reference: House format - one loud driver defends a single thesis (was 'the-take')

series_dna.spine: Defends one committed thesis to the death and dares the audience to disagree.

slots.substitution: recast the driver from the cast pool - this is a solo format by design

cast_logic.relationship_physics: host vs the audience's anticipated objection

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: accusation - the thesis stated in the first ten seconds, no wind-up

branches.note: evidence-run uses the three strongest receipts only

episode_grammar.escalation_curve: the dare sharpens - the host names the objection the viewer is typing and answers it; concessions exist only to set up counterpunches
episode_grammar.payoff: the thesis restated harder + a direct dare

formats.name: RAPID WIRE
formats.reference: House format - fast roundup + call-in drop-ins (was 'hot-wire')

series_dna.spine: Rips through the day's items fast and never apologizes for cutting one off.

slots.substitution: recast the wire host from the cast pool
solo host carries the wire
OPTIONAL_MODULE: drop the call-in; add one more wire item

cast_logic.relationship_physics: straight-comic; the call-in is a distinct outsider character interrupted freely

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: stakes_announce - what the wire is carrying today, rapid-fire list
episode_grammar.escalation_curve: the pace itself is the pressure; no item over 60s, hardest first; the call-in is the spike
episode_grammar.payoff: the one thing worth watching, named
episode_grammar.notes: the call-in character is an editorial choice (an outsider voice). Its phone-bandwidth SOUND is a rendering property and lives in the production skin / that voice's design, not here.

formats.name: NEWS DESK
formats.reference: House format - the nightly multi-story anchor desk (was 'the-desk')

series_dna.spine: Builds the night's lead as a case, then works down the desk to the last word.

slots.substitution: recast the anchor from the cast pool; the show does not run without its anchor seat
OPTIONAL_PROOF: read the drop-in's prior on-record statement as an ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM, or cut the interview

cast_logic.relationship_physics: anchor-led, with an optional per-block drop-in that confirms or extends a story

episode_grammar.entry_ritual: artifact - open on the lead story's defining receipt
episode_grammar.escalation_curve: the lead builds context -> receipts -> the turn; each block ends one step short so the audience closes the loop
episode_grammar.payoff: the anchor's last word: a committed verdict + what to watch tomorrow
episode_grammar.notes: measured, never shouty; direct address to the audience; rhetorical questions the anchor answers; the c-block is the lighter culture / birthday / follow-up item.
